title.narrative: Provision of emergency protection services including prevention and response of CRSV/GBV among IDP and host community women and girls in Amhara region and contested areas.

description.narrative: Humanitarian emergencies exacerbate existing vulnerabilities and disproportionately impact women and girls, who often face increased risks of violence, exploitation, and discrimination. These crises disrupt protective social structures and services, leading, for example to heightened exposure to gender-based violence with limited access to essential services, fewer economic opportunities for women and women-led households specifically, and women-led organizations tend to not be included nor consulted during a response. The inclusion of UN Women in CERF UFE allocations is crucial to ensure a comprehensive response that addresses these unique and critical needs, protecting the lives and dignity of affected women and girls, as part of CERF’s aim to deliver Effective Programming in: a) Localization; b) Protection: GBV Programming; Target GBV funding for WLOs; WLOs in GBV Programming, AAP and PSEA; c) Gender Equality (GAM marker; Gender Equality programme focus); and d) People with Disabilities.Ethiopia faces complex humanitarian crises occasioned by conflicts and prolonged drought which have resulted into a severe humanitarian hardship with millions of IDPs, chronic malnutrition, food insecurity, high risk and vulnerability. During the conflict, horrendous gender-based violence (GBV) targeting women and girls has been committed by armed groups and civilians. Though unreported GBV cases are numerous, a recent study in the region shows that 43.3% (2,241/5,171) of women experienced at least one type of GBV. Of the sexual violence survivors, rape alone accounted for 82.2% of cases, of which 68.4% reported being gang raped; and young women (aged 15–24 years) were the most affected by sexual violence, 29.2%. Commonly reported SGBV-related issues were physical trauma, sexually transmitted infections, HIV infection, unwanted pregnancy, and depression. Additionally, flooding, locust infestations, and inflation [29.2%] are exacerbating food insecurity. The suspension of food aid by USAID has affected 20 million people, leading to hunger-related deaths in Tigray, including women. Therefore, the overarching goal of the proposed project under CERF_UFE is to strengthen the Provision of emergency lifesaving protection services including prevention and response of CRSV/GBV among IDP/returnees and host community women and girls in North Wollo (Raya Kobo), Wag Hamra (Sekota town), South Gondar (Sedie, Muja, and Simada), and contested areas including Alamata town, Mai Tsebri town, Raya Alamata and Zata. UN Women will strengthen and establishes women empowerment approach called: Women’s Empowerment centers (WECs) in humanitarian response. This approach which UN Women has implemented in other countries’ humanitarian response including through CERF -UFE could really be more holistic and effective in responding to the protection needs of women, adolescent girls experiencing serious hardship and high protection risk in targeted zones in Amhara region and contested areas. UN Women will be engaging women led and women right organization with strong presence in the targeted project sites and with an ongoing UN Women staff at Field level through rigorous project monitoring and supportive supervision. Whereby, overall project implementation will be led by WLOs/WROs. WLOs/WRO will be covering the Amhara (South Gondar-Seden Muja and Simada), and contested (Mai Tsebri, Alamata town, Raya and Zata), targeted region and contested areas respectively. Majorly, WLO/WROs will be participating in the direct project intervention in the Provision of emergency lifesaving protection services including prevention and response of CRSV/GBV among IDP/returnees and host community women and girls in South Gondar), and contested areas including Alamata town, Mai Tsebri town, Raya Alamata and Zata.
